allowed.reason: Adds network.denyMachLookup: macOS Mach services denied at the end of the Seatbelt profile, where they win over srt's built-in allows. sandbox-srt uses it to deny com.apple.SecurityServer and com.apple.securityd.xpc to the untrusted profile, so code in the fence can't read the Keychain (attack case A36, design HAL-958 section 6, HAL-6346). srt has allowMachLookup but no way to take a service away. Also keeps the Windows egress check's loopback probe from failing: srt binds an ephemeral port outside the proxy range [60080,60089] in 5 attempts, closing each one in the range, and Windows hands out ports in sequence, so a start that lands at 60080 fails every attempt. The patch keeps those listeners open until it finds a port outside the range, with one attempt more than the range has ports (HAL-7431). Also adds --report-fd to srt's command line: srt writes the violation line of each network request its proxy refused to an inherited descriptor (displaced with /dev/null for the program on Linux and macOS, as --control-fd is; on Windows the inheritable handle reaches the program unnamed, so sandbox-srt reads every line as untrusted), so sandbox-srt can report blocked sites to the run page. srt keeps these lines in its violation store, which its command line never shows (HAL-12648). And it starts srt-win hidden on Windows (windowsHide on the CLI's spawn): the agent host runs without a console, so without it every sandboxed command opened a console window (HAL-13197).
allowed.remove-when: Each part can go on its own: the Mach-service denies when srt can deny a Mach service itself (proposed upstream) or sandbox-srt no longer runs on Seatbelt; the port search when srt's verifyWindowsWfpEgress finds a port outside the range by itself, or sandbox-srt no longer runs on Windows; the report fd when srt's command line reports refused requests itself, or sandbox-srt runs srt as a library; the windowsHide when srt's CLI starts srt-win hidden itself

allowed.reason: Runs at most 8 `git log --follow` processes at a time in getCommitsThatAddFiles, keeping the input order. Unpatched, `changeset version` starts one per pending changeset, all at once: with 591 changesets on main that peaked at 5.6 GB locally and 8.5 to 9.4 GB in Fast gates' `pnpm version-packages`, which our CI server killed at its 10 GB ceiling (HAL-15966). Patched, it peaks at 2.2 GB whatever the number of changesets, and writes the same changelogs.
allowed.remove-when: @changesets/git limits how many git processes getCommitsThatAddFiles runs at once, or finds the commits with a single git call
